name: Question 12
problem: The position $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\sqrt{2}t,\,t,\,{t}^{3}⟩,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1\,\text{s}.$
worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t=1,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{2},\,1,\,3{t}^{2}⟩ \\ v(1) & =⟨\sqrt{2},\,1,\,3(1)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{2},\,1,\,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t=1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,6t⟩ \\ a(1) & =⟨0,\,0,\,6(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(1)\cdot a(1)$ and $||v(1)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1)\cdot a(1) & =⟨\sqrt{2},\,1,\,3⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,6⟩ \\  & =18 \\ ||v(1)|| & =\sqrt{(\sqrt{2})^{2}+{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{12} \\  & =2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=1$, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(1)\cdot a(1)}{||v(1)||} \\  & =\frac{18}{2\sqrt{3}} \\  & =3\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $3\sqrt{3}\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

Question 12
?

The position r, in meters, of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨2t,t,t3⟩, where t is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of P at time t=1s.

a
 36ms−2
b
 33ms−2
c
 26ms−2
d
 93ms−2
e
 3ms−2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The tangential component of acceleration is given by aT=v⋅a||v||.

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at t=1, as follows: v=⟨ddt(2t),ddt(t),ddt(t3)⟩=⟨2,1,3t2⟩v(1)=⟨2,1,3(1)2⟩=⟨2,1,3⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at t=1: a=⟨ddt(2),ddt(1),ddt(3t2)⟩=⟨0,0,6t⟩a(1)=⟨0,0,6(1)⟩=⟨0,0,6⟩.

Then, we compute v(1)⋅a(1) and ||v(1)||:

v(1)⋅a(1)=⟨2,1,3⟩⋅⟨0,0,6⟩=18||v(1)||=(2)2+12+32=12=23

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at t=1, and we get aT=v(1)⋅a(1)||v(1)||=1823=33.

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is 33ms−2.
